title: EI-TR: A Versatile Exponential Integrator Framework for Transient Analysis of Generic Nonlinear Circuits
problem: Application of exponential integrator (EI) methods to generic nonlinear circuits faces numerical instability and difficulty in combining with Newton iterations.
motivation: To provide a more efficient and stable alternative to backward differentiation formulas (BDF) for transient circuit simulation.
method: Novel nonlinear EI framework with implicit regularization using smart eigenvalue modification to avoid system partition that induces numerical instability; truncated rational (TR) approximation for nonlinear function treatment. Decouples linear and nonlinear system solutions and reduces three-layer nested iteration in EI-NK to single Newton loop similar to conventional BDF.
key_novelty: Implicit regularization scheme with TR approximation enabling stable exponential integration for generic nonlinear circuits.
contributions: Novel EI-TR framework for generic nonlinear circuit transient analysis
Implicit regularization scheme avoiding system partition instability
3× reduction in Newton iterations compared to EI-NK
6.5× larger time steps compared to traditional trapezoidal methods
limitations: The approach is specific to transient circuit simulation and may require adaptation for other EDA applications.
